transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-09
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes (recording captured)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Dylan Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Kestrel Head of Platform), Liam O'Rourke (DevOps), Sara Mendes (ML Eng), Noah Park (Security)

Summary: quick discovery on integration pattern options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), SDK and gateway/proxy model, LangChain/LlamaIndex usage patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer wants low-latency inference for interactive product plus an occasional high-throughput batch rerank.

Topics: rollout options, VPC networking, KMS/HSM, tracing, KV cache behaviour, SDK language support, LangChain adapters, token cost control, canary strategy, and benchmark plan.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um, this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. we also have Dylan from SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Priya: hi, Priya here. thanks for making time. quick context, Kestrel is building an interactive knowledge assistant embedded in our ops console, target latency under 300ms for short prompts, and we also run nightly reranks for recommendations where throughput matters.
[00:22] Liam: yeah and we're sensitive to egress costs and want to keep PII inside our VPC where possible.
[00:28] Dylan: great, that's helpful. just to orient, we'll cover our hosted API, Dedicated/reserved capacity, and Private (V P C / on-prem) options. and then dig into integration patterns — SDKs, gateway/proxy, and common langchain/llamaindex adapters. anything to add?
[00:40] Sara: also curious about how KV cache and continuous batching behave with short-turn (chat) requests vs bulk rerank jobs.
[00:47] Maya: perfect — we'll walk that through. quick question on timelines and success criteria — what would a successful POC look like for you?
[00:55] Priya: POC ideally shows we can hit 300ms p95 for interactive prompts on Dedicated, and a monthly cost projection for expected 150M tokens/month. also need a security review pass — SOC 2 + K M S integration.
[01:08] Noah: yes security is critical. we need to verify key management (H S M) and audit logs before we touch any sensitive data.
[01:15] Dylan: understood. from a tech fit, two common approaches we see: 1) keep control plane in Redwood hosted and use dedicated capacity for predictable latency — minimal infra work, 2) Private deployment (V P C or on-prem) where you bring your own network and K M S — more lift but full data control. we can also do a hybrid — hosted control plane + private serving nodes.
[01:35] Liam: hybrid sounds interesting. how does routing work if we have both Hosted and Private? fallback?
[01:40] Dylan: yes you can set policies — route low-latency traffic to Dedicated/private and fallback to hosted variants of the model if capacity is exhausted. routing supports region and cost policies too. there is a small additional latency when falling back because of model variant mismatch but it's typically acceptable for non-critical flows.
[01:58] Priya: when you say model variant mismatch, do you mean quantized vs full fp16 and potential quality diffs?
[02:05] Dylan: exactly. we have verified performance profiles per model and can recommend quantization profiles for batch vs interactive. in practice you can pin quality thresholds and fall back to higher-cost variants for specific routes.
[02:18] Maya: let's talk SDKs — we support python/ts/java SDKs and first-class integrations for LangChain and a LlamaIndex connector. are you planning to use either?
[02:27] Sara: our team uses LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). we also have a custom gateway between our front-end and backends.
[02:35] Dylan: perfect. the LangChain adapter is pretty thin — you can swap in Redwood's llm wrapper and we support streaming responses, tool-calls, and function-like structured outputs. for LlamaIndex we expose a simple client that hooks into the index retriever. sometimes customers front this with an internal gateway or proxy to centralize auth and rate limiting.
[02:55] Liam: speaking of rate limits — we need per-team quotas and hard throttles to protect other services, and also token-level billing visibility. do you expose rate-limit hooks?
[03:05] Dylan: yes — Redwood Console exposes per-route quotas and token budgets. you can enforce hard limits in the gateway or configure soft quotas with alerts. we also provide webhooks for limit breach events and an API to query usage so your gateway can do preemptive throttling.
[03:22] Priya: is there an easy way to auth from an internal gateway to Redwood without embedding keys in client bundles?
[03:28] Maya: common pattern is gateway-to-Redwood using short-lived service tokens and mTLS between your gateway and our private endpoint. for Hosted you can also use VPC peering + private endpoint and keep keys only on backend.
[03:40] Noah: for compliance — do you provide tenant-specific audit logs and the raw request logs for SOC 2? and how long are logs retained by default?
[03:48] Dylan: tenant logs are available; default retention is 90 days but enterprise packages can extend retention. audit logs include token-level usage, request headers, and model decisions. for Private deployments you control storage and retention.
[04:02] Sara: curious about observability — we use Datadog and OpenTelemetry. can Redwood export traces and metrics?
[04:10] Dylan: yes, we have a tracing hook that emits OpenTelemetry spans and you can forward metrics to Datadog or Prometheus. we also surface per-request traces in the Console and let you attach your correlation IDs (x-request-id) so you can correlate frontend traces with model latency and cost.
[04:27] Maya: real quick on latency breakdown — we provide token-level timing, network hop estimates, and GPU queueing metrics. this helps pinpoint whether p95 spikes are due to batching or network.
[04:38] Liam: about batching — will automatic batching impact tail latency for the interactive path? we can't have user-facing jitter.
[04:45] Dylan: Redwood's runtime supports workload-aware batching. for strict p95 targets you can opt out of batching for the interactive route or set max batching window to extremely low values, and use prefix/KV caching to reduce tokens. the Optimize tool can recommend batching configs from a sample workload.
[05:04] Priya: what's the expected engineering lift to get up and running for Private? we have strict network egress policies.
[05:11] Dylan: Private deployment typically involves network admins and security — setting up VPC peering, routing, and K M S integration. for a small pilot, we provide an infra runbook and a deployment image; expect 2-4 weeks with your infra team for initial validation. Dedicated is usually faster since it's managed — we just provision reserved capacity and configure your network rules.
[05:30] Sara: any limitations with LlamaIndex compatibility? sometimes embeddings call patterns differ and we need to pipeline embeddings + index updates.
[05:37] Dylan: embeddings are supported and you can push them through our batch ingestion APIs. we provide client-side helpers to throttle and backoff. LlamaIndex connector supports incremental updates; we recommend using our SDK to batch embedding calls to optimize throughput and cost.
[05:52] Maya: on pricing — we'll send a preliminary cost model but generally Hosted is usage-based, Dedicated has a monthly committed capacity price, and Private combines a platform fee plus dedicated capacity. you'll get token + compute breakdowns in the Console.
[06:05] Priya: for the POC we'll probably request both Dedicated and Private cost options to compare.
[06:12] Noah: one more on keys — does Redwood support customer-managed keys in cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) or do you require our keys to be on-prem H S M?
[06:20] Dylan: we support cloud KMS and H S M depending on deployment. Hosted supports bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via a customer-managed KMS. Private gives you total control and can integrate with on-prem H S M. we'll share the KMS integration doc.
[06:32] Liam: what about maintenance windows and upgrades? we need predictable change windows for our integrations.
[06:37] Maya: for Dedicated we'll negotiate maintenance SLAs; Private lets you control upgrade timing. Hosted has scheduled maintenance with notice and can support blackout windows for high-criticality customers under enterprise terms.
[06:51] Priya: can we run a short benchmark — say 500 concurrent interactive users with 3-turn average sessions — to validate p95?
[06:58] Dylan: yes. action: we'll send a benchmark template and you can run it against a small Dedicated pool. we'll also help run tests from our side if you want.
[07:07] Sara: how do we instrument function/tool-calls and structured outputs? our RAG pipeline depends on structured responses to extract entity lists.
[07:15] Dylan: the SDK supports function-like outputs and schema enforcement. you can pass a JSON schema and the model will attempt to conform; the Console also offers structured-output validators and regression alerts if schema drift is detected.
[07:30] Maya: circling back to gateway patterns — many customers front Redwood with an internal API gateway that centralizes auth, caching, and rate limits. that gateway then talks to Redwood's private endpoint with mTLS. do you have an example repo?
[07:42] Dylan: yes, we'll share a sample gateway implementation (node/express + envoy) and a config for short-lived service tokens. link: https://redwood.ai/examples/gateway-onramp (note: shorthand link in call).
[07:56] Liam: ok great. about quota enforcement — can we do per-team budgets that reset monthly and also per-route hard throttles?
[08:03] Dylan: yes both are supported. you can tie quotas to API keys or to upstream gateway identities if you proxy requests. the Console shows spend by token and you can set notifications on thresholds.
[08:14] Priya: any gotchas around cold-start for the model instances — e.g., when switching to a new variant during a fallback?
[08:21] Dylan: cold-start is mostly a warm-up time for model weights loading. we support pre-warming and keep-alive pools for Dedicated. for Private you can set desired min replicas to avoid cold starts. fallbacks to hosted variants might incur a small latency hit during the first few requests as the JVM/serving process warms.
[08:41] Maya: do customers commonly use Redis or our prefix cache for RAG?
[08:46] Sara: we use Redis for retrieval cache right now. curious if Redwood's prefix cache integrates with existing Redis clusters?
[08:54] Dylan: ours is internal to the runtime but you can replicate cache invalidation hooks to your Redis. for Private deployments it's easier to integrate directly.
[09:01] Liam: on observability again — we'd want span correlation. what's the header key?
[09:06] Dylan: x-redwood-request-id for our traces, and we accept x-request-id as a passthrough to correlate. the SDK attaches basic tracing automatically if you pass an OTEL tracer.
[09:18] Priya: let's discuss data residency briefly — we need EU-only residency for a subset of tenants. can Redwood restrict model serving to eu-west regions?
[09:27] Dylan: yes, region pinning is possible. for Hosted we can region-restrict; Dedicated can be provisioned in a customer-preferred region; Private is obviously in your datacenter or VPC region. we'll add region constraints to the POC plan.
[09:39] Maya: quick note on security docs — we'll send SOC 2, ISO attestation summary, and our KMS/HSM integration guide after the call.
[09:48] Noah: great. also want to confirm penetration testing windows — we do scheduled pen tests quarterly. what are the constraints?
[09:56] Dylan: for Hosted we have an approved pen-test process and require coordination; Dedicated/private give you more control — we can schedule approved windows and provide contact.
[10:06] Priya: ok, next i'd like to capture a rough POC plan and owners.
[10:12] Maya: proposed POC: 2-week Dedicated pilot with 2 GPU nodes sized for low-latency, run Redwood benchmark script for interactive and batch workloads, validate K M S integration and audit logs, and a follow-up security review. owners: Dylan for benchmarks, Maya for commercial, Priya/noah on customer side.
[10:28] Liam: timeline? we can kick off infra work next week if we get the runbook.
[10:32] Maya: we'll send the runbook and a benchmark template today, and aim to start pilot the following week.
[10:39] Sara: one more question — do you have any automatic quality/regression alerts for prompt sets? we'll want to know if we change prompts and cause quality drift.
[10:47] Dylan: yes, Redwood Optimize supports prompt/eval sets and will raise regression alerts. you can tie alerts to canary rollouts so you only promote models passing your eval thresholds.
[10:57] Priya: sounds good. anything else on integrations?
[11:00] Maya: the only other item is SDK language support for our mobile clients — we recommend proxying from mobile to your gateway to avoid exposing tokens.
[11:09] Liam: noted.
[11:12] Dylan: ok i'll recap the immediate action items.
[11:16] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the V P C/K M S deep dive.
[11:21] Priya: thanks — appreciate it.

Recap (end of call):
- POC: 2-week Dedicated pilot + benchmark (owners: Dylan, Maya, Priya)
- Deliverables: benchmark template, private deployment playbook, pricing/sizing options, KMS integration doc, sample gateway repo
- Security: schedule V P C/K M S deep dive with Noah (proposed 2026-05-13)
